oracle.efficient: answer(): per block floor((10^k-1)/a)+1 - (floor(((b+1)p-1)/a) - floor((bp-1)/a)), p=10^(k-1), Python floor of -1//a handles b=0; running product mod 10^9+7.
independent: band_oracle(): sum over leading digits d != b of ceil-based multiple counts in [d*p,(d+1)*p-1], pairwise product tree mod 10^9+7 (every extras case, every official test and sample)

enumerated_count()/leading_histogram(): steps through every multiple of a in [0,10^k) and reads the leading digit of the zero-padded decimal string (all a,b for k<=4 in brute_checks; official/extras with k<=5 / k<=4)
phone_brute(): enumerates every digit string of length n<=4, splits into blocks and checks int(block) % a == 0 and block[0] != b
exact big-integer product of enumerated per-block counts reduced once at the end (300 multi-block cases, m<=300)

problem.title: Pasha and Phone

semantics: Three lines: n k (1<=n<=100000, 1<=k<=min(n,9), k divides n); m=n/k values a_i with 1<=a_i<10^k; m digits b_i in 0..9 (exponents attested from the public English statement). A block is the k-digit zero-padded integer, so its first digit is 0 for values below 10^(k-1). Unique integer: product over blocks of (multiples of a_i in [0,10^k-1]) minus (multiples in [b_i*10^(k-1),(b_i+1)*10^(k-1)-1]), modulo 10^9+7. Floor-difference oracle; independently checked by per-leading-digit ceil counts, zero-padded multiple enumeration for every a_i,b_i with k<=4, and literal phone-number enumeration n<=4.
